h33-h33-2-b2-MASSm10minus-20261023-71329.hypothesis: R0's dots that sit in the near-catalogue collar carry less credit than the metric's break-even, so deleting them raises DTI even though some are close to known traces.
h33-h33-2-b2-MASSm10minus-20261023-71329.mechanism: Binary-dot algebra (vendor/gems57/metric.py): DTI = T/(0.2*(T+n-M)+0.8|G|). Removing one dot lowers the denominator by exactly 0.2 regardless of its credit, so a removal gains iff that dot's realised credit to unseen truth is below 0.2*DTI = 0.0556 at DTI 0.2778. The removed set is concentrated in the collar, which is the region where the 0.2708->0.2778 prune paid.
h33-h33-2-b2-MASSm10minus-20261023-71329.ranking_basis: 0.6*clip(d_catalogue_px/50) + 0.4*uniform(seed88). This is NOT the parent's model ranking: R0's score field is not stored anywhere (every H33-lineage raster is binary). 40% of the score is uniform noise and 20% of parent dots saturate the distance term at 1.0.

h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.hypothesis: At a fixed dot count, raising local dot density on the parent's most confident km-scale clusters raises the metric more than the relocation costs, because the metric's false-positive term is sum_x p(x)(1 - max_g k): a dot welded next to an already-covering dot pays almost no penalty (0.2(1 - k) ~ 0.07 at 1 px) while a dot in an empty km block pays the full 0.2. Mass moved out of the coldest blocks therefore relieves denominator weight that the parent was still paying.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.mechanism: DTI = T / (0.2T + 0.2(n - M) + 0.8|G|) with n fixed at 37654. Each move changes the denominator by 0.2(t_add - t_rm + m_rm - m_add). Donors are drawn from the coldest 1 km blocks (mean block prior 0.75 dots/km2) where m_rm ~ 0; receivers land in blocks with mean prior 2.54 dots/km2 at 1.04 px from a surviving host, so m_add is inherited from the host's proximity to truth. No new pixels enter the catalogue collar and no block is emptied.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan benches and GeoDAWN E-W flight-line corrugation both survive edge filters and pack into km-scale bands; welding dots onto them raises M only if the host is actually near truth, so a mimic shows up as a null (m_add ~ 0), not a false gain. Conversely, alluvial geothermal outflow along range fronts forms km-scale clusters with no fault slip, which would produce a real m_add but nothing in T.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.predicted_sign_size: MODEL +0.011 live, scenario range [-0.002, +0.030]. Point scenario: m_add 0.30, t_rm 0.02, m_rm 0.02, t_add = 0.2 m_add, calibrated on the two CLAIM pairs (0.2778 / 0.2600). The sign is not guaranteed: at m_add <= 0.15 and t_rm >= 0.02 the recall lost from the donors dominates.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.confounder: CV excursion. Under every estimator tried, R0 sits at 0.62 (raw 1 km counts, occupied blocks) / 0.48 (5 km-smoothed density); these variants push it to 1.02-1.36 / 0.67-1.07, far outside the 0.51-0.59 band the brief quotes for the best files. If that band is causal and not an artefact of the estimator, the live change should be negative even though the algebra predicts positive. That is the cleanest way to falsify the folklore.
h33-h33-2-b2-CONCb10px-m10-20261023-89ff.falsifier: Live change <= -0.010: concentration past the parent costs real recall, the cold-tail donors were catching isolated blind faults, and the axis is closed. Live change in (-0.010, +0.010): the metric's redundancy credit is too small to matter at 10-20 % and the axis is closed as sub-noise at this dose. Live change >= +0.010 with the 20 % move > 10 % move: mechanism confirmed, scale the dose and combine with the best MASS setting next session.

h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E1-20261023-01cf9e98.hypothesis: R0's dots sit on the H19-5 ridge field, not on the geophysical anomaly; moving each dot at most 2 px onto the local maximum of the magnetic/gravity gradient magnitude re-centres it on the basement step a new fault actually produces, and DTI inside the 300 m kernel pays for that re-centring.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E1-20261023-01cf9e98.mechanism: Fault-parallel basement offset -> density and susceptibility contrast -> horizontal-gradient maximum of rtp magnetics and isostatic gravity. GeoDAWN Area 2 was flown at 400 m line spacing and 150-200 m drape (https://data.usgs.gov/datacatalog/data/USGS:657e1d85d34e23d3533209f7), so a potential-field edge maximum can sit 1-3 px off the mapped trace. The dot count is held fixed, so any change is credit-only (T and M), never mass.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E1-20261023-01cf9e98.non_fault_mimic: Basalt-flow margins, Lake Lahontan shorelines and welded-tuff caprock boundaries produce gradient maxima with no Quaternary fault; E-W GeoDAWN flight-line corrugation is a pixel-scale artefact, which is why both fields are pre-smoothed before differencing.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E1-20261023-01cf9e98.predicted_sign_size: A-priori +0.004. Post-build the paired SGMC blind-fault PROXY fell 0.00796, so the shipped MODEL prediction is -0.002 (range [-0.010, +0.006]): the SGMC delta attenuated by ~0.25 because SGMC is compiled at a different scale from the scored new-fault truth. Below the 0.01 evidence bar either way.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E1-20261023-01cf9e98.falsifier: A live change of +0.01 or more (recovering the lost blind-fault proximity) falsifies the negative PROXY; a live change between -0.01 and +0.01 confirms SNAP is not a lever at this window, which retires the axis for the remaining slots.

h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2S2-20261023-60ced8c7.hypothesis: The negative SGMC result for w2E1 is noise-chasing, not a failure of the edge idea: at 1 px smoothing the within-window maximum is dominated by pixel-scale detector noise, so the same snap on a 200 m-scale edge, gated to moves with a real gain (>= 0.25 robust-z), should keep whatever structural signal exists.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2S2-20261023-60ced8c7.mechanism: Gaussian smoothing at sigma = 2 px (200 m) suppresses single-pixel corrugation while leaving basement-step gradients 200-600 m wide intact. The gain gate then only moves a dot when the destination is a distinct local maximum rather than a marginal noisy neighbour, which is why 52% rather than 95% of dots move.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2S2-20261023-60ced8c7.non_fault_mimic: Smoothing also smears adjacent parallel lineaments together, so a dot can be dragged onto the wrong strand of a fault zone; alluvial-fan surface breaks still produce edges at this scale.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2S2-20261023-60ced8c7.predicted_sign_size: MODEL -0.001 (range [-0.009, +0.007]): half of the w2E1 blind-fault loss, consistent with the measured SGMC delta of -0.00396 vs -0.00796, so most but not all of the w2E1 damage is pixel noise.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2S2-20261023-60ced8c7.falsifier: If w2S2 scores below w2E1 live, the noise hypothesis is wrong and the loss comes from leaving the parent's ridge geometry, not from edge noise; if it scores above w2E1 by more than 0.01 the edge idea survives and a coherence-weighted SNAP deserves a slot.

h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E2-20261023-861cd355.hypothesis: The operator choice does not matter: the organizer's own derivative bands should give the same result as a recomputed gradient if the effect (negative or positive) is physical rather than an artefact of my smoothing.
h33-h33-2-b2-SNAPw2E2-20261023-861cd355.mechanism: Bands 3 (tmi_hg), 9 (tmi_vg) and 18 (iso_grav_anom_hg) are already first derivatives, so their magnitudes peak over the same basement steps as E1 while skipping a second differencing step.
